_: Questions whose business vocabulary shares no stem with the identifiers they are about.
This set exists because #121 asked for a measurement the fixed question set cannot
make: every question there uses the schema's own words, so a selector that bridges no
vocabulary gap still scores perfectly on it. Each entry here asks its twin's question
out of a different vocabulary — turnover rather than revenue, parcels rather than
shipments, depots rather than locations — and reuses the twin's reference spec, since
the expected result is the same rows whatever the question called them.
What is deliberately not here is a fix. Choosing between a synonym index, a model-
assisted first call and embeddings is gated on the live baseline in #61, so this set
measures the current selector's behaviour and records it; tests/test_vocabulary.py
holds the record current. Run with:

questions.name: turnover_by_country
questions.question: Which ten countries generated the most turnover? Count an order's value as turnover, count only orders placed on or after 1 January 2025, and leave out orders that were cancelled or refunded.
questions.notes: Turnover for revenue and value for total; neither stem appears in any identifier. The reference is the plain-language twin's.

questions.name: purchases_per_month
questions.question: How many purchases were made in each month? Leave out purchases that carry no purchase date.
questions.notes: Purchases for orders and purchase date for order date; 'month' names nothing in the schema either way.

questions.name: overall_turnover
questions.question: What was the overall turnover, counting an order's value as turnover, over orders placed on or after 1 January 2025 that were not cancelled or refunded?
questions.notes: 'Overall' rather than 'total' keeps even the aggregate noun out of the match.

questions.name: refunds_by_cause
questions.question: How many refunds were requested for each cause of refund?
questions.notes: Refunds for returns and cause for reason — the two nouns a person outside the schema would reach for first.

questions.name: parcels_per_courier
questions.question: How many parcels did each courier firm handle? Parcels whose courier reference matches no courier firm are their own group rather than dropped.
questions.notes: Parcels for shipments and courier for carrier. The left-join sentence is kept, because the twin's reference is a left join and the expected rows are the same rows.

questions.name: delivery_charge_trend
questions.question: What was the typical delivery charge per month? Leave out deliveries that have not been sent yet.
questions.notes: Delivery charge for shipping cost and sent for shipped; 'typical' stands in for average without naming an aggregate the schema could match.

questions.name: reads_by_depot
questions.question: Which ten depots recorded the most barcode reads?
questions.notes: Depots for locations and barcode reads for shipment scans; the ten is what makes this the twin's question rather than a different one.
